items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Paul was working with Lewis Armstrong

ctx.x: Is that Edna? No, not Edna.

No, not Edna. Willamina something. Willamina Borg. Yeah, Willamina Borg, yeah, yeah. So, uh, Danny was working up there and he hadn't so long, hadn't too long got married. And, uh, like he got married working on that job, yeah. So, he was good friends with Lee and also I was good friends with Danny, you know. So, they had a trip, this fella Sherman Cooks had a trip to, had an excursion trip to go to Chicago, you see. And, uh, Lewis Armstrong at the time was living in Chicago, you see. And, uh, Lee was telling me,…
You never did join the WPA band then?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: not working, but I mean getting jobs with Emma Barrett and Paul Barberin and, uh, Noon and the Bazooka Man.

ctx.x: And when I came back, well, that's where I start, uh, working with, uh, not working, but I mean getting jobs with Emma Barrett and Paul Barberin and, uh, Noon and the Bazooka Man.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: I played with him with Paul Bobbler. When he had the Dixie Land Hall on Boyle Street

ctx.x: I don't have much work for it.

I was with Cotter when he first started out. They had a recording couple come down here and record it. He wanted him. Well, I was playing guitar then. I got the album riding in some way. Well, we'd been high, you know, just a long time. I played with him with Paul Bobbler. When he had the Dixie Land Hall on Boyle Street, I know you can remember that. He was with that. And, and he was with the band, with the Puyon band, like I told you. and he was playing songs there, I played the wrong time, but it all come back…
